Replace every line below. Nothing here is a checklist and there is nothing to
tick: a ticked box records that somebody read a line, and the point of this
template is to record what a machine printed. Paste output, not confidence.
-->

## The issue

<!-- `Closes #<n>` where this finishes the issue, `Refs #<n>` where it does not.
     A change with no issue behind it does not have a shape anybody agreed to
     yet, and the issue is where that argument belongs. -->

Closes #

## What changed

<!-- What a reader will see in the diff, in the order it makes sense to read
     it. One topic. Where the change carries a second unrelated thing, it is two
     pull requests. -->

## What failure it prevents

<!-- The thing that could go wrong and now cannot, or the thing that was already
     wrong. Where this is a correction, say what was wrong and how it was found,
     because how it was found is what stops the same defect arriving again by
     another route. -->

## The means, and why it fits

<!-- One sentence naming the language, format or tool this change is made of and
     why that is the right one for this artefact. Not carried over from the last
     change, because a means that suited that one is an assumption about this
     one. Where the means was forced from outside, name what forced it. -->

## What was run, and what it printed

<!-- The commands, at the commit being pushed, with their output pasted. Not a
     description of having run them.

     Where something was not run, say that it was not run and why, and leave the
     sentence negative. A line admitting a check did not happen is worth more
     than a line implying it did.

     Where the change adds a guard, this is where the proof that it bites goes:
     the fixture that makes it refuse, and the run where removing the guard
     makes the same fixture pass. -->
